descriptor: Multi-banner food retailer (Ahold USA/Food Lion/Stop&Shop + Albert Heijn/Delhaize) · 52/53-week FY ends late Dec · reported in EUR millions

kpis.note: IFRS reported margin; a 0.1-0.2pp move is a real story at this scale

sections.title: Growth & Margin
sections.subtitle: Revenue growth is steady but slow; the entire investment case rides on a ~3-4.4% operating margin, so a few tenths of a point matter more than the top line. FY2016 is a merger stub (Delhaize consolidated only from 24-Jul-2016, ~5 months) — exclude it from any growth read. FY2016/2020/2026 are 53-week years.

charts.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
charts.annotation: FY2016→FY2017 (+26.6%) is the Delhaize merger consolidating for a full year, not organic growth.

charts.title: Operating Margin: Reported vs Underlying
charts.annotation: Underlying margin strips restructuring, impairments and one-offs (e.g. FY2020's Giant Food pension settlement) — it is the company's own guided measure and sits slightly above reported margin in most years.

charts.title: Gross Margin
charts.annotation: Gaps are FY2016, FY2019, FY2020 and FY2023: cost of revenue was not disclosed in a comparable form in the source filings for those years — the chart skips them rather than plotting zero.

sections.title: Segments, Online & Comparable Sales
sections.subtitle: The US and Europe segments are run as near-independent businesses (different banners, currencies and margin structures); online and like-for-like comparable sales are the growth engines inside a mature store base. Segment and online figures are disclosed annually only.

charts.title: Revenue by Segment: US vs Europe
charts.annotation: FY2025: US €53.1bn (57.5% of group) vs Europe €39.3bn (42.5%) — Europe grew faster in FY2025 (Profi/Romania + FX) while US comps have been the softer segment recently.

charts.title: Segment Operating Margin: US vs Europe
Online Sales & Share of Group Revenue
charts.annotation: Online sales reached €10.3bn in FY2025 (11.1% of group revenue), up from €2.0bn (4.0%) in FY2016 — mostly grocery e-commerce and meal-kit/on-demand delivery, not a marketplace GMV figure.

charts.title: Comparable Sales Growth (Like-for-Like)
charts.annotation: Like-for-like sales at constant store count and currency — the volume/price measure a grocer discloses instead of same-store units. FY2020 and FY2022 spikes are COVID pantry-loading and inflation pass-through respectively, not durable growth.

sections.title: Cash Generation & Shareholder Returns
sections.subtitle: The equity story is per-share compounding: a stable free cash flow stream funds both the dividend and a buyback that has cut the share count by 30% since FY2016.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Reported FCF already deducts lease principal repayments and net interest — it is NOT OCF minus capex (FY2025: reported €2,600m vs OCF−capex €4,425m). Owner FCF is the DCF's own build (reported FCF + interest paid − interest received − SBC), used to keep every year on one consistent basis back to FY2017; FY2016 is excluded as a merger stub.

charts.title: Shares Outstanding
charts.annotation: 1,272m (FY2016) → 887m (FY2025), a ~30% reduction funded by ~€1bn/yr of buybacks — the main lever behind EPS growth outpacing net income growth.

charts.title: Total Debt & Cash
charts.annotation: TotalDebt is NOT comparable before/after FY2018: IFRS-16 lease capitalisation added €7.25bn of gross debt in one step (€7,250m FY2017 → €14,485m FY2018) with no change in the underlying business — read the pre/post-2018 levels as two different series.

sections.title: Quarterly Seasonality (Q1 2023 – Q2 2026)
sections.subtitle: Discrete quarters (not year-to-date) since Q1 2023. Q4 is seasonally the strongest quarter on US holiday and European year-end trading.

charts.title: Quarterly Revenue & Margin
charts.annotation: Margin is seasonally lowest in Q3/Q4 2023-2024 and has been recovering through 2025-2026 on cost actions and easing inflation.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total net sales across all banners in the US and Europe segments, reported in EUR.

For Ahold Delhaize: revenue growth is low-single-digit and driven by a mix of comparable sales, new store openings, online growth and currency translation (the US segment reports in USD, so EUR/USD moves swing consolidated growth even with flat underlying US performance).

What to watch:

  • FY2016 is a merger stub — Delhaize consolidated from 24-Jul-2016 only, so FY2017's +26.6% is not organic
  • FY2016, FY2020 and FY2026 are 53-week fiscal years, adding ~1.5-2pp of extra-week growth
  • EUR/USD translation, not just underlying sales, moves the US segment's EUR-reported revenue

operatingMargin.title: Operating Margin: Reported vs Underlying
operatingMargin.content:
Operating income divided by revenue, on both the IFRS-reported basis and the company's own underlying (non-GAAP) basis.

For Ahold Delhaize: this is the single most important number in the business — a mature, thin-margin grocer that has held underlying operating margin in a narrow 3.8-4.8% band for a decade. A 0.2-0.3pp move is a material swing in profitability.

What to watch:

  • Underlying margin excludes restructuring charges, impairments and one-off items (e.g. FY2020's Giant Food multi-employer pension settlement)
  • Management's FY2026 guidance targets ~4% underlying operating margin
  • Price investment (management has flagged ~€1bn) and SNAP benefit cuts are live downside risks to margin, not revenue

netMargin.title: Net Margin
netMargin.content:
Net income divided by revenue.

For Ahold Delhaize: tracks operating margin closely but is noisier — tax items, associates' income and discrete one-offs (e.g. the FY2020 pension settlement) move it more than the underlying business.

What to watch:

  • Compare against operating margin to see whether a move is operational or below-the-line

grossMargin.title: Gross Margin
grossMargin.content:
Revenue less cost of goods sold, divided by revenue.

For Ahold Delhaize: stable at ~26.5-27.5%, typical for a supermarket operator competing on price. Chart has gaps in FY2016, FY2019, FY2020 and FY2023 because cost of revenue was not disclosed in a comparable form for those years — the chart skips these points rather than plotting a false zero.

What to watch:

  • A grocer's gross margin moves on private-label mix, promotional intensity and supplier terms, not volume

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by Segment: US vs Europe
segmentRevenue.content:
Group revenue split between the United States segment (Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Giant, Hannaford) and the Europe segment (Albert Heijn, Delhaize, bol, and Central & Southeastern Europe banners).

For Ahold Delhaize: the US is the larger segment (~57.5% of FY2025 revenue) but Europe has been growing faster recently on Profi (Romania) and FX. The two segments have different currencies, competitive dynamics (US: Walmart/Kroger/discounters; Europe: Aldi/Lidl/Jumbo) and margin structures.

What to watch:

  • US segment revenue is reported in EUR after USD translation — EUR/USD moves affect the split even with flat underlying performance
  • Segment figures are disclosed annually only, not quarterly, in this dataset

segmentMargin.title: Segment Operating Margin: US vs Europe
segmentMargin.content:
Segment operating income divided by segment revenue, derived from the disclosed segment figures.

For Ahold Delhaize: the US segment has historically run a higher margin than Europe, though Europe closed much of the gap in FY2025.

What to watch:

  • This is a derived ratio from disclosed segment revenue and segment operating income, not a separately reported margin line
  • SNAP (US federal food-assistance) enrollment changes are a US-segment-specific risk not shared by Europe

onlineSales.title: Online Sales & Share of Group Revenue
onlineSales.content:
Company-disclosed online/e-commerce sales across both segments — primarily online grocery ordering and delivery (bol marketplace sales in the Netherlands are reported separately and are not included here).

For Ahold Delhaize: online sales reached €10.3bn in FY2025, 11.1% of group revenue, more than 5x FY2016's €2.0bn (4.0% of revenue) — one of the clearer structural growth vectors in an otherwise low-growth business.

What to watch:

  • This is the company's own disclosed online sales figure, not a marketplace GMV — it is included within, not additional to, total group revenue
  • Online grocery typically carries a lower margin than in-store until delivery density scales

comparableSales.title: Comparable Sales Growth (Like-for-Like)
comparableSales.content:
Sales growth at stores open more than a year, at constant currency, excluding gasoline — the grocery-industry equivalent of same-store sales.

For Ahold Delhaize: the cleanest read of underlying volume and price/mix performance, isolated from new store openings, closures and FX.

What to watch:

  • FY2020 spikes (13.3% US, 9.5% Europe) are COVID pantry-loading, not durable
  • FY2022's elevated readings (7.4% US, 2.9% Europe) are inflation pass-through, not volume growth
  • FY2024's US slowdown to 0.5% preceded the FY2025 SNAP-related and price-investment pressures management has flagged

fcf.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
fcf.content:
Three different earnings/cash measures on one chart: statutory net income, the company's own reported free cash flow, and the owner FCF used as the DCF's base.

For Ahold Delhaize: reported FCF is the company's own definition — it deducts gross capex, lease principal repayments and net interest paid, and is materially lower than a naive OCF-minus-capex calculation (FY2025: €2,600m reported vs €4,425m OCF−capex). This is deliberate: a lease-heavy grocer's lease payments are a real, unavoidable cash cost, not optional financing.

What to watch:

  • Never compare Ahold Delhaize's reported FCF to a peer's OCF-minus-capex figure without adjusting for lease treatment
  • Owner FCF (used in the DCF) starts from reported FCF and adds back interest paid and removes interest received and SBC, for a consistent FY2017-2025 series (FY2016 excluded as a merger stub)

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Period-end common shares outstanding.

For Ahold Delhaize: fell from 1,272m (FY2016) to 887m (FY2025), a ~30% reduction funded by roughly €1bn/yr of buybacks alongside a maintained and growing dividend — the core per-share compounding mechanism in the equity story.

What to watch:

  • Buybacks are treated in the DCF as value-neutral capital return (held flat, not modelled as accretion), not as a growth driver
  • SBC is small here (~0.08% of revenue) so dilution from equity awards is immaterial

eps.title: EPS & Dividend Per Share
eps.content:
Basic earnings per share and the annual dividend per share, both in EUR.

For Ahold Delhaize: EPS growth has outpaced net income growth because of the falling share count; the dividend has risen most years, funded by the stable free cash flow stream.

What to watch:

  • FY2020 EPS is depressed by the Giant Food FELRA/MAP multi-employer pension settlement, a one-off, not an operating deterioration
  • Payout ratio (dividend / EPS) has generally run 45-55%

debt.title: Total Debt & Cash
debt.content:
Total debt (including lease liabilities) and cash and cash equivalents at period end.

For Ahold Delhaize: total debt jumped from €7,250m (FY2017) to €14,485m (FY2018) purely from IFRS-16 lease capitalisation — leases that were previously off-balance-sheet operating commitments became on-balance-sheet debt with an offsetting right-of-use asset, with no change to the underlying business or its cash flows.

What to watch:

  • Never compare pre-FY2018 and post-FY2018 total debt directly — they are measuring different things
  • The DCF's own net debt figure excludes most lease liabilities from the leverage measure since lease costs are already charged once in the owner-FCF flows (see the valuation section for the exact bridge)

quarterlySeasonality.title: Quarterly Revenue & Margin
quarterlySeasonality.content:
Discrete (non-cumulative) quarterly revenue and operating margin, Q1 2023 onward.

For Ahold Delhaize: Q4 is seasonally the strongest revenue quarter (US holiday season, European year-end trading); margin has been recovering through 2025-2026 from a 2023-2024 trough.

What to watch:

  • Always compare a quarter to the same quarter a year earlier, never to the immediately preceding quarter
  • These are discrete quarters reconstructed from interim filings, not year-to-date cumulative figures

dcf.base_sublabel: Company-defined FCF, adjusted for interest & SBC
